seat.BEST_WHY: The timber band along the top wall (y≈420–455, x≈185–500 and x≈565–720) is built from planks of unequal width with driven pins at irregular spacing (x≈300, 395, 455), so it reads as repaired by hand rather than tiled. Floor stones vary in length within a course (the course at y≈560–600 runs roughly 55px, 90px, 40px) and joints are offset course to course. The pale pillar at x≈262–298 carries a hide strap near its base (y≈615–625), which is the fiction's repair language made physical. The crate (x≈190–300, y≈475–515) and the bound log pair (x≈380–500, y≈590–640) sit wholly on floor tiles and do not cross a wall boundary. The lantern falloff has no banding, and the brazier's glow is warmer and weaker than the lantern, so the two sources are distinguishable.
seat.WORST_WHY: The pool at x≈250–343, y≈0–190 is a flat teal fill with a repeating hexagonal scale pattern, and its border with the dirt is a straight one‑pixel edge with no bank, lip or shadow. The grey wall caps are identical tiles with uniform one‑pixel light joints on a perfect grid (left column x≈0–55, bottom band y≈205–265). The same teal moss decal is stamped at three places (x≈20–45, y≈55–80; x≈15–40, y≈215–235; x≈360–380, y≈150–175). The two barrels at y≈195–225 are pixel‑identical. The dirt floor is uniform speckle noise with stray saturated blue pixels (around x≈150–200, y≈150–170 and x≈190, y≈115). There is no light falloff anywhere; every tile is at full value, so the "only light" conceit is absent.

flip_list: The wall top surfaces (olive plane above the timber band x≈185–500, y≈380–420; the vertical run x≈440–505, y≈85–400; the right wedge x≈565–750, y≈330–420) are soft cloud‑noise fills with no masonry; draw them as coursed cap stones at the same pixel density as the floor.

The floor crack is one continuous 1px curve (x≈210,y≈625 to x≈470,y≈530, with a second arc x≈560–690, y≈640–700) that crosses stone joints without deflecting or changing width; redraw cracks so they follow joints, vary in width, and have a lit edge on the lantern side.
The three barricades at x≈185–305, y≈655–710 are the same sprite stamped three times at equal spacing; make each one different (stake length, lean, a missing member, a rope wrap on one only).
The hero sprite is at 2x pixel size with a black outline while the floor is at 1x and the props are smooth‑shaded; put all three on one pixel grid.

The pillar at x≈262–298 has a top‑left highlight and the barricades keep saturated orange four tiles into the dark; light props from the figure's lantern and apply the same falloff to them as to the floor.
No prop has a contact shadow (pillar base, barricades, brazier); add a short dark contact shadow on the side away from the figure.
The brazier glow (centre x≈598, y≈548) is a soft disc with a visible circular boundary about 40px out; lengthen the falloff or break the disc with the stone pattern.
The dark scribble marks on the lit stones near x≈400–470, y≈500–560 read as glyph‑like noise ("2", "T" shapes); replace with chips, pits and wear that follow the stone edges.

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.
